rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exodus says Moses tended Jethro’s sheep, but the Qur’an has no purpose in specifying that work.
rows.anchor: وورد في سفر الخروج أنه رعى غنم يثرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not specify wages; on its apparent reading, the payment is marriage to the daughter, while otherwise customary tribal wages are left unstated because the story has no need to detail them.
rows.anchor: وقد علمت أن الظاهر أنه إنكاحه البنت فإذا لم نأخذ بهذا الظاهر كانت الآية غير متعرضة للأجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author recalls that shepherds in the early 14th century received an annual shirt, shoes called balagha, and other items as customary compensation.
rows.anchor: أن راعي الغنم له في كل عام قميص وحذاء يسمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extra two years are left to Moses as a favor, according to his inclination when the eight-year term ends.
rows.anchor: جعل ذلك إلى موسى تفضلا منه أن اختاره ووكله إلى ما تكون عليه حاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min is partitive in origin, and ʿinda is figuratively the self; the omitted predicate means completion of ten is from Moses, not the employer, so it is outside the bilateral contract.
rows.anchor: و ( من ) ابتدائية . و ( عند ) مستعملة في الذات والنفس مجازا

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik cites the father’s offer without a reported request for the daughter’s consent as evidence that a father may marry off his virgin daughter without her permission.
rows.anchor: واحتج مالك بقوله { إني أريد أن أنكحك إحدى ابنتي هاتين } على أن للأب إنكاح ابنته البكر

rows.speaker: من يمنع ذلك
rows.claim: Opponents answer that the verse’s silence about seeking permission does not prove that permission was not obtained.
rows.anchor: ولمن يمنع ذلك أن يقول : إن عدم التعرض له لا يقتضي عدم وقوعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿayb means he will be righteous in dealing with people through good treatment and gentleness, thereby showing Moses his character.
rows.anchor: يريد الصالحين بالناس في حسن المعاملة ولين الجانب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This self-description is not forbidden self-praise: praise is blameworthy when intended for boasting, whereas a religious or practical purpose is a good motive, as in Joseph’s request at 12:55.
rows.anchor: ليس هذا من تزكية النفس المنهي عنه لأن المنهي عنه ما قصد به قائله الفخر والتمدح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashuq means to impose hardship; attributing the hardship to the speaker is figurative because he would be its cause, meaning he will not stipulate a burdensome condition.
rows.anchor: أكون شاقا عليك ، أي مكلفك مشقة ، والمشقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The assurance of leniency accords with the hadith praising a person who is gracious when selling and buying; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وهذا من السماحة الوارد فيها حديث : ( رحم الله امرأ سمحا إذا باع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses accepts Shuʿayb’s terms, and this response completes both the marriage and employment agreements: the arrangement stands as stipulated.
rows.anchor: حكاية لجواب موسى عن كلام شعيب . واسم الإشارة إلى المذكور وهو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Between me and you is figurative language for firm obligation and mutual commitment, each party being responsible for his part.
rows.anchor: وأطلق { بيني وبينك } مجازا في معنى الثبوت واللزوم والارتباط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ayyamā is accusative under qaḍayt; ayy is an indefinite relative like mā, and the added mā emphasizes its ambiguity, making it general and condition-like with a conditional answer.
rows.anchor: و { أيما } منصوب ب { قضيت } . و ( أي ) اسم موصول مبهم مثل ( ما )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The whole clause is a circumstantial-substitution apposition to “that is between us,” since choice of the term’s endpoint is part of the agreement.
rows.anchor: والجملة كلها بدل اشتمال من جملة { ذلك بيني وبينك } لأن التخيير في منتهى الأجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With ʿayn vowelled in the noun, ʿudwān means violating a right; Moses negates every kind of such violation, including any by the employer.
rows.anchor: والعدوان بضم العين : الاعتداء على الحق ، أي فلا تعتدي علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses calls God to witness against both himself and Shuʿayb; as their entrusted guarantor of the covenant, God can hold either accountable for breach.
rows.anchor: واستشهد موسى على نفسه وعلى شعيب بشهادة الله . وأصل الوكيل : الذي وكل إليه الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here wakīl includes the sense of witness, so it takes ʿalā rather than its usual preposition ilā.
rows.anchor: ولما ضمن الوكيل معنى الشاهد عدي بحرف { على } وكان حقه أن يعدى ب ( إلى )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not destroy towns except when their people wrong themselves through associating partners with God; shirk is the cause and sending a messenger is its precondition, with denial completing their wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: أي ما كان من عادتنا في عبادنا أن نهلك أهل القرى في حالة إلا في حالة ظلمهم أنفسهم بالإشراك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Their people being wrongdoers” is a circumstantial clause, the sole surviving state after an ellipsis required by the restrictive exception.
rows.anchor: وجملة { وأهلها ظالمون } في موضع الحال ، وهو حال مستثنى من أحوال محذوفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse follows the reminder of Meccan security and provision: worldly goods are temporary, while the afterlife is better and enduring, so believers should seek it through faith even if guidance costs them worldly advantages.
rows.anchor: هذا وجه مناسبة هذه الآية لما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min shayʾ clarifies the general “whatever you have been given”; the context makes the referent beneficial things, since giving commonly means granting what benefits.
rows.anchor: و { من شيء } بيان ل { ما أوتيتم } والمراد من أشياء المنافع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording shifts from speaking of them in the third person to addressing them directly because the preceding speech calls for face-to-face reproach.
rows.anchor: وقد التفت الكلام من الغيبة من قوله { أو لم نمكن لهم حرما } ( القصص : 57 ) إلى الخطاب في قوله { أوتيتم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Matāʿ is something enjoyed for a time and then lost.
rows.anchor: والمتاع : ما ينتفع به زمنا ثم يزول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zīna means what makes bodies or things beautiful.
rows.anchor: والزينة : ما يحسن الأجسام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is better in the quality and completeness of its kinds of blessings, and more enduring because it is everlasting.
rows.anchor: أن أجناس الآخرة خير مما أوتوه في كمال أجناسها ، وأما كونه أبقى فهو بمعنى الخلود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing question reproaches them and presses them to acknowledge their failure to use sound reason, treating them as if their minds were impaired.
rows.anchor: وتفرع على هذا الخبر استفهام توبيخي وتقريري على عدم عقل المخاطبين

rows.speaker: الجمهور; أبو عمرو ويعقوب
rows.claim: Most readers have taʿqilūn with second-person tāʾ; Abū ʿAmr and Yaʿqūb read yaʿqilūn with third-person yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { تعقلون } بتاء الخطاب . وقرأ أبو عمرو ويعقوب { يعقلون } بياء الغيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third-person reading may turn from direct address so believers marvel at the polytheists, or treat them as absent because their lack of reason puts them far from direct address.
rows.anchor: على الالتفات عن خطابهم لتعجب المؤمنين من حالهم ، وقيل : لأنهم لما كانوا لا يعقلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author thinks the connective fa introduces the contrast because polytheists flaunted wealth and luxury while most Muslims were poor; the transient worldly lot contrasts with the believers’ lasting reward and the disbelievers’ punishment.
rows.anchor: أحسب أن موقع فاء التفريع هنا أن مما أومأ إليه قوله { وما أوتيتم من شيء

words: ثُمَّ هُوَ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ مِنَ ٱلْمُحْضَرِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people receiving the good promise are believers, while those brought to punishment are the disbelievers; the comparison denies that the two groups are equal.
rows.anchor: فما صدق { من } الأولى هم الذين وعدهم الله الوعد الحسن وهم المؤمنون ، وما صدق { من } الثانية جمع هم الكافرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause “he will meet it” is parenthetical reassurance that the promise is certain, and its fa expresses consequence.
rows.anchor: وجملة { فهو لاقيه } معترضة لبيان أنه وعد محقق ، والفاء للتسبب

words: ثُمَّ هُوَ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ مِنَ ٱلْمُحْضَرِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final clause coordinates with “We gave him worldly enjoyment” as part of the relative clause; thumma marks a rise in rank of the loss.
rows.anchor: وجملة { ثم هو } الخ عطف على جملة { متعناه متاع الحياة الدنيا } فهي من تمام صلة الموصول . و { ثم } للتراخي الرتبي

words: ثُمَّ هُوَ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ مِنَ ٱلْمُحْضَرِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their loss exceeds missing the afterlife’s delights: they are instead repaid with painful punishment.
rows.anchor: لم تقتصر خسارتهم على حرمانهم من نعيم الآخرة بل تجاوزت إلى التعويض بالعذاب الأليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comment that the spider’s house is the weakest is an explanatory aside and proverb for futility; it likens non-Islamic worship to contemptible, misguided religions, though their errors vary in degree.
rows.anchor: وجملة { وإن أوهن البيوت لبيت العنكبوت } معترضة مبينة وجه الشبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “If they knew” attaches to the spider comparison, not the statement about the web’s weakness; its implied result is that they would recognize their likeness, but they do not know their idols are useless.
rows.anchor: وجملة { لو كانوا يعلمون } متصلة بجملة { كمثل العنكبوت } لا بجملة { وإن أوهن البيوت لبيت العنكبوت }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After saying they fail to know their idols’ worthlessness, God declares knowledge of their detailed conditions and beliefs, and uses the parable to expose their poor judgment and call them to examine realities; compare 2:216.
rows.anchor: أعقبه بإعلامهم بعلمه بدقائق أحوال تلك الأصنام على اختلافها واختلاف معتقدات القبائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā may be negative and suspend yaʿlamu, with min extra for emphasis; the genitive phrase is semantically the object of tadʿūn, yielding “you invoke no existent thing.”
rows.anchor: يجوز أن تكون نافية معلقة فعل { يعلم } عن العمل ، وتكون { من } زائدة لتوكيد النفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording depicts the idols as nonentities, devoid of divine attributes and of the benefit their worshippers claim; it does not deny that they actually invoke them.
rows.anchor: أن الله يعلم أنكم لا تدعون موجودا ولكنكم تدعون أمورا عدمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent denial of existence is figurative, like saying Christians “are not on anything” or the Prophet’s saying that soothsayers “are nothing” with respect to their claimed knowledge of the unseen.
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى { ليست النصارى على شيء } في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some among the People of the Book and Meccans who believe the Qur’an nevertheless conceal that belief and deny it because they are entrenched in disbelief.
rows.anchor: أن من هؤلاء الذين يؤمنون بالقرآن من أهل الكتاب وأهل مكة من يكتم إيمانه جحودا منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article marks the fullest degree of the quality: only those deeply rooted in disbelief deny the signs, avoiding the tautology that deniers are merely deniers.
rows.anchor: فالتعريف في { الكافرون } للدلالة على معنى الكمال في الوصف المعرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is called signs because its inimitability challenges opponents, who cannot produce a comparable sūra; this first addresses actual polytheist deniers and prepares a possible later address to the People of the Book without accusing them in advance.
rows.anchor: وعبر عن { الكتاب } ب ( الآيات ) لأنه آيات دالة على أنه من عند الله بسبب إعجازه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s known illiteracy is powerful evidence that revelation came from God; the Qur’an elsewhere also invokes his prior lack of knowledge of scripture and his lifetime among his people.
rows.anchor: هذا استدلال بصفة الأمية المعروف بها الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم ودلالتها على أنه موحى إليه من الله أعظم دلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He had not read any book before the Qur’an, preventing anyone from claiming it was drawn from books he had previously recited.
rows.anchor: أنك لم تكن تقرأ كتابا حتى يقول أحد : هذا القرآن الذي جاء به هو مما كان يتلوه من قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse also denies writing any book, even without reciting one, excluding both routes of learning and fully establishing illiteracy; a memorizer who cannot write and a copyist who lacks learned knowledge are not considered illiterate.
rows.anchor: فالمقصود نفي حالتي التعلم ، وهما التعلم بالقراءة والتعلم بالكتابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idhan is the response and consequence of an implicit law condition inferred from the Prophet’s not reading or writing: had he done either before, falsifiers would have doubted.
rows.anchor: جواب وجزاء لشرط مقدر ب ( لو ) لأنه مفروض دل عليه قوله

rows.speaker: المرزوقي
rows.claim: Al-Marzūqī reads the second hemistich of Qurayẓ al-ʿAnbarī’s poem as answering an imagined question about what Banū Māzin would do if the camels were raided.
rows.anchor: قال المرزوقي في ( شرح الحماسة ) : ( إذن ) هو أنه أخرج البيت الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author also allows “then they would have supported me” to answer the implicit law condition, as if it were a second answer; similarly, “if free, I would condemn slaves’ deeds; then I would admire free men’s deeds.”
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون أيضا : إذن لقام ، جواب ( لو ) كأنه أجيب بجوابين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Irtiyāb means the occurrence of doubt in the mind.
rows.anchor: والارتياب : حصول الريب في النفس وهو الشك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prior reading or writing could have raised a suspicion that the Qur’an came from earlier books or material he had copied; this would invite preliminary doubt, not justify certainty of denial, since its style and meaning refute the suspicion after reflection.
rows.anchor: لو كان ذلك واقعا لاحتمل عندهم أن يكون القرآن من جنس ما كان يتلوه من قبل من كتب سالفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “With your right hand” emphasizes writing, since writing is done by the right hand, like the Qur’an’s “no bird that flies with its wings” at 6:38.
rows.anchor: وتقييد تخطه } بقيد { بيمينك } للتأكيد لأن الخط لا يكون إلا باليمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are called people of falsehood because their denial is baseless; the description signals that they are deeply immersed in falsehood, paralleling “the disbelievers” in the prior verse.
rows.anchor: ووصف المكذبين بالمبطلين منظور فيه لحالهم في الواقع لأنهم كذبوا مع انتفاء شبهة الكذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bal cancels the hypothetical that falsifiers might doubt: the Qur’an is unmistakably from God, its verbal and semantic inimitability proves the Prophet’s truth, and his illiteracy corroborates it.
rows.anchor: أي بل القرآن لا ريب يتطرقه في أنه من عند الله ، فهو كله آيات دالة على صدق الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author’s preferred referent for the breasts of those given knowledge is the Prophet’s own breast, with the plural serving to honor him; the knowledge bestowed is prophethood, as in David and Solomon’s knowledge at 27:15.
rows.anchor: فالمراد من : { صدور الذين أوتوا العلم } صدر للنبيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is in the Prophet’s heart as each passage descends; it may then be written by revelation scribes and recited after descent, since only pre-revelation reading is denied.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الآية أن كونه في صدر النبيصلى الله عليه وسلم هو شأن كل ما ينزل من القرآن

rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr cites a report from Zayd ibn Thābit about 4:95 as evidence that scribes wrote a verse while it was being revealed; he gives no grading.
rows.anchor: كما دل عليه حديث زيد بن ثابت في قوله تعالى : { لا يستوي القاعدون من المؤمنين غير أولي الضرر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of revelation entering the Prophet’s heart is linked to the Spirit’s descent upon his heart and to revelation strengthening his heart.
rows.anchor: كما قال : { نزل به الروح الأمين على قلبك } ( الشعراء : 193 ، 194 ) وقال : كذلك لنثبت به فؤادك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the preferred reading of the sentence, “in the breasts” is a second predicate of the pronoun: the Qur’an was placed in the Prophet’s breast and is clear signs.
rows.anchor: ولهذا فالوجه أن يكون الجار والمجرور في قوله : { في صدور الذين أوتوا العلم } خبرا ثانيا عن الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible referent is the breasts of the Prophet’s companions and Muslim memorizers; then the phrase completes praise of the Qur’an, and the prepositional phrase modifies “clear signs.”
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد ب { صدور الذين أوتوا العلم } صدور أصحاب النبيصلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurbā means kinship by lineage and womb; miskīn is cross-referenced to the poor and needy in 9:60, and ibn al-sabīl is a traveler passing through a village or encampment.
rows.anchor: وابن السبيل : المسافر المجتاز بالقرية أو بالحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The right is left general, with its meaning supplied by customary practice and the Prophet’s explanation.
rows.anchor: ووقع الحق مجملا والحوالة في بيانه على ما هو متعارف بين الناس وعلى ما يبينه النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before the Hijra, charity was generally obligatory and left to believers’ conscientiousness; it was called zakat in many Meccan verses, often paired with prayer, without fixed recipients or amounts, then later regulated by categories and measures.
rows.anchor: وكانت الصدقة قبل الهجرة واجبة على الجملة موكولة إلى حرص المؤمن

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
rows.claim: Abū Bakr said that zakat is a due on wealth.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه : فإن الزكاة حق المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once prescribed zakat was specified after the Hijra, other charity ceased to be obligatory and was called ṣadaqa or birr; the general financial rights of these three groups belonged to early Islam and were superseded by formal zakat.
rows.anchor: وإنما ضبطت بعد الهجرة فصار ما عداها من الصدقة غير واجب . وقصر اسم الزكاة على الواجبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A relative’s right varies with need: a wealthy relative merits a conciliatory gift, while a needy one has a stronger claim; here the likely referent is a financially weak relative not yet poor, while a rich relative’s gift is recommended kindness rather than this right.
rows.anchor: فحق ذي القربى يختلف بحسب حاجته ؛ فللغني حقه في الإهداء توددا ، وللمحتاج حق أقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poor person’s right is to have his need met.
rows.anchor: وحق المسكين : سد خلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The traveler’s right is hospitality, as in the hadith that a guest’s due is one day and night; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وحق ابن السبيل : الضيافة كما في الحديث ( جائزته يوم وليلة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command counters pagan customs of giving to distant people for praise and to prominent figures for favor, and recalls the duty to bequeath fairly to parents and relatives at 2:180.
rows.anchor: والمقصود إبطال عادة أهل الجاهلية إذ كانوا يؤثرون البعيد على القريب في الإهداء والإيصاء حبا للمدحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That is better” points back to giving the relative his due, and face-seeking means giving to obey God and earn His reward.
rows.anchor: والإشارة بقوله { ذلك خير } إلى الإيتاء المأخوذ من قوله { فئاتت ذا القربى حقه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s face figuratively presents the gift as given in His sight; it also echoes pagan giving to high-status people’s faces, now redirected to God, meaning obedience and seeking His pleasure.
rows.anchor: وذكر الوجه هنا تمثيل كأن المعطي أعطى المال بمرأى من الله لأن الوجه هو محل النظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khayr may be comparative, better than pagan showy giving to wealthy outsiders or than usury, or it may mean goodness in the sense of God’s reward for believers.
rows.anchor: و { خير } يجوز أن يكون تفضيلا والمفضل عليه مفهوم من السياق أن ذلك خير من صنيع أهل الجاهلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The separating pronoun creates an additional restriction: those giving to the named recipients for God’s sake alone are the successful; showy or boastful giving brings no success.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله وأولئك هم المفلحون } صيغة قصر من أجل ضمير الفصل ، وهو قصر إضافي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After urging support for needy kin and the resulting success, the passage discourages usury, common in pre-Islamic and early Islamic times especially among Thaqīf and Quraysh; exploiting a needy borrower contradicts mutual aid.
rows.anchor: لما جرى الترغيب والأمر ببذل المال لذوي الحاجة وصلة الرحم وما في ذلك من الفلاح أعقب بالتزهيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā is a general conditional, and the sentence is an inserted qualification after the preceding command; it warns of blameworthy giving and addresses God-seeking Muslims who used to lend at interest before its prohibition.
rows.anchor: و { ما } شرطية تفيد العموم ، فالجملة معترضة بعد جملة { فئاتت ذا القربى حقه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “You gave” means some of you gave to others, since giving entails both a donor and a recipient.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { ءاتيتم : } آتى بعضكم بعضا لأن الإيتاء يقتضي معطيا وآخذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address in “so that it may increase” is directed to the party receiving the usurious gain.
rows.anchor: وقوله { لتربوا في أموال الناس } خطاب للفريق الآخذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tarbu means to increase your own wealth; fī is figurative for “from,” so the profits are gained from other people’s assets.
rows.anchor: و { لتربوا } لتزيدوا ، أي لأنفسكم أموالا على أموالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poet Sabr al-Faqʿasī uses fī in the sense “from” in “we drink and gamble from their prices”; the same usage occurs in “provide for them therein and clothe them” at 4:5.
rows.anchor: قول سبرة الفقعسي : ونشرب في أثمانها ونقامر أي نشرب ونقامر من أثمان إبلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min in both “from usury” and “from alms” explains the ambiguity of the two instances of general mā; usury was discussed earlier in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: ومن } في قوله { من ربا } وقوله { من زكاة } بيانية مبينة لإبهام { ما } الشرطية في الموضعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional answer means the interest does not grow in God’s estimation: it is deficient and blameworthy; this reading keeps ribā in its familiar sense and fits 2:276, the doubled language here, and 3:130.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { فلا يربو عند الله } أنه عمل ناقص عند الله غير زاكك عنده ، والنقص يكنى به عن المذمة والتحقير

rows.speaker: السدي والحسن
rows.claim: Al-Suddī and al-Ḥasan transmit the interpretation that the usurious gain is deficient and blameworthy with God.
rows.anchor: وهذا المعنى مروي عن السدي والحسن . وقد استقام بتوجيهه المعنى

rows.speaker: جم غفير من المفسرين
rows.claim: Many commentators take ribā to mean a gift to wealthy people meant to increase their favor or holdings, including reciprocal, ingratiating, or flattering gifts; the aim is to show such giving earns no divine approval.
rows.anchor: ودرج على هذا المعنى جم غفير من المفسرين فيصير المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the alternative gift reading, “so that you increase” restates the intended increase and thereby attaches the phrase to “in people’s wealth.”
rows.anchor: وتصير كلمة { لتربوا } توكيدا لفظيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about alms returns to the preceding command to give the relative his due, since that right is called zakat.
rows.anchor: رجوع إلى قوله { فئاتت ذا القربى حقه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final clause answers the alms condition: its givers are those whose reward is multiplied; the separating pronoun restricts that title rhetorically to them, disregarding transient worldly gains, and the demonstrative honors them.
rows.anchor: وجملة { فأولئك هم المضعفون } جواب { وما ءاتيتم من زكاة ، } أي فمؤتوه المضعفون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The increase is multiplied reward, and the demonstrative in place of a pronoun honors those who give alms for God’s sake.
rows.anchor: وهو إضعاف الثواب . وضمير الفصل لقصر جنس المضعفين على هؤلاء
